advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider warning/erroring when `--ref` is supplied on a non-close transition, since it is silently ignored there.
evidence: `ref` is parsed unconditionally in `_parse_flags` and threaded to `transition_compute`/`close_ticket`, but only read inside the `target_status == 'closed'` completion-gate path (transition_close.py:611-671)
ABSENCE: no validation or warning that `--ref` is a no-op for non-close targets
advisory.finding: `--ref` / `ref=` is silently accepted and ignored on non-close transitions (it is only consumed in the close path); an operator passing `--ref=<sha>` on e.g. `open in_progress` gets no error and no effect.
scenarios: Operator supplies `--ref` on a non-close transition expecting it to matter and is silently ignored

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting `_parse_flags(["--ref"])` raises CommandError('Error: --ref requires a value') with returncode 1.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:170: `raise CommandError("Error: --ref requires a value", returncode=1)`
ABSENCE: search for '--ref requires a value' finds only the source raise, no test assertion
advisory.finding: The new `--ref requires a value` error branch (raised when `--ref` is the final arg with no following value) is untested; no test asserts the CommandError/returncode for a trailing bare `--ref`.
scenarios: Operator invokes `rebar transition <id> closed --ref` with no ref value; parser must reject with a clear error
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `with pytest.raises(CommandError): _transition._parse_flags(["--ref"])` and assert the message/returncode.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test closing a story with `--ref=<nonexistent-ref>` and assert it fails-closed (raises, no signature) rather than crashing or signing.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:669: `_fresh_sha = resolve_ref(ref, str(config.repo_root(repo_root)), fetch=False)` — real call added by this change
Sibling suite shows an unresolvable ref raises SnapshotRefError: tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_attested_signing.py:211 `with pytest.raises(SnapshotRefError):`
ABSENCE: both new tests pass only valid SHAs (sha1) to `ref=`; no test passes a bogus ref through the close path
advisory.finding: No test covers a `--ref`-targeted close where the ref is unresolvable/invalid; the stub's `resolve_ref(ref or "HEAD", ...)` is always handed a real SHA, so the drift-guard's real `resolve_ref(ref, ...)` call (transition_close.py:669) and the real verifier's ref-resolution error path are never exercised for the new `--ref` input.
scenarios: Operator passes a typo'd or non-existent commit to `--ref`; the close gate must fail-closed rather than sign against a bad target or crash unexpectedly in the drift guard

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Wrap the `--ref` `resolve_ref` drift-guard call so an unresolvable ref degrades to the closed-without-signature warning (matching the HEAD/head_sha 'never raises' posture) instead of raising post-close.
evidence: src/rebar/signing.py:511-525: `head_sha` returns `'unknown'` on failure and 'never raises' by contract

transition_close.py:642-645 comment: 'A crash in this (two-local-commit) window leaves closed-without-signature' — but the subsequent SigningError handler (lines 683-691) only wraps `sign_completion_verdict`, not the `resolve_ref` call at 669
dropped.finding: In the post-close pre-sign drift guard, the `--ref` branch calls `resolve_ref(ref, ..., fetch=False)` which raises `SnapshotRefError` on an unresolvable ref, but this runs AFTER the close has already committed and is not wrapped in try/except — unlike the HEAD path (`signing.head_sha`) which returns 'unknown' and never raises. An unresolvable ref in the verify→close→sign window therefore crashes with an unhandled exception instead of degrading to the intended 'closed WITHOUT completion signature' warning.
scenarios: A `--ref=<sha>` close where the ref became unresolvable between verify and sign (e.g. concurrent GC/prune, or a branch/ref deleted in the window)
A ref that resolved only via a want-fetch at verify time but is not in the local object DB for the fetch=False re-read
dropped.suggested_fix: Catch `SnapshotRefError` around the `resolve_ref` call and treat it like `head_sha`'s 'unknown' (set `_fresh_sha = "unknown"` so `_material_drifted` returns False / or emit the drift warning), so the post-close window never raises.
